stage.definition: The platform or area where a performance is presented.
stage.exampleUsage: The performers entered the stage for the final scene.

spotlight.definition: A strong focused light that shines on one part of a stage.
spotlight.exampleUsage: The spotlight illuminated one part of the stage.

backdrop.definition: A background placed behind a subject or scene.
backdrop.exampleUsage: The backdrop formed the background of the scene.

trapdoor.definition: An opening with a movable cover in a stage floor.
trapdoor.exampleUsage: The approved set design includes a covered trapdoor in the stage floor.

wings.definition: A stage area out of sight of the audience.
wings.exampleUsage: The performer waited in the wings before entering.

proscenium.definition: The stage opening or frame separating the stage area from the auditorium in a proscenium theater.
proscenium.exampleUsage: The proscenium frames the audience's view of the stage.

fly-system.definition: A system of ropes, cables, pulleys, and supports in a theater used by trained crews to raise and lower scenery or equipment above the stage.
fly-system.exampleUsage: Only trained crew operate the fly system.

cyclorama.definition: A large background surface or cloth at the rear of a stage, often curved.
cyclorama.exampleUsage: The cyclorama provided the large background surface.

auditorium.definition: The part of a theater where the audience watches the performance.
auditorium.exampleUsage: The audience entered the auditorium before the performance.

orchestra-seats.definition: Audience seats on the main floor of a theater, usually closest to the stage.
orchestra-seats.exampleUsage: The orchestra seats are on the theater's main audience floor.

balcony.definition: An upper floor projecting from the rear over the main floor in an auditorium.
balcony.exampleUsage: The visitor's seat was in the upper balcony.

box-seat.definition: A prized seat in an enclosed theater box or an elevated section of a sports stand.
box-seat.exampleUsage: The ticket was for a box seat in the separate theater box.

aisle.definition: Passageway between seating areas as in an auditorium or passenger vehicle or between areas of shelves of goods as in stores.
aisle.exampleUsage: The usher directed visitors along the aisle.

row.definition: An arrangement of objects or people side by side in a line.
row.exampleUsage: The ticket identified the booked row.

lobby.definition: The theater’s entrance or reception area.
lobby.exampleUsage: Visitors waited in the lobby before admission.

box-office.definition: The place where tickets for a theater or event are sold or collected.
box-office.exampleUsage: The visitor collected the ticket at the box office.

cloakroom.definition: A room or staffed area where visitors leave coats.
cloakroom.exampleUsage: The visitor left a coat at the cloakroom.

program.definition: A printed or digital account of a performance, its cast or schedule.
program.exampleUsage: The program lists the performers and production details.

costume.definition: The attire worn in a play or at a fancy dress ball.
costume.exampleUsage: The performer wore the costume selected for the character.

wig.definition: Hairpiece covering the head and made of real or synthetic hair.
wig.exampleUsage: The wig changed the character's hair appearance.

mask.definition: A covering to disguise or conceal the face.
mask.exampleUsage: The mask formed part of the costume design.

cape.definition: A sleeveless garment hanging from the shoulders.
cape.exampleUsage: The cape hung from the performer's shoulders.

crown.definition: A decorative headpiece worn by a performer portraying royalty.
crown.exampleUsage: The crown identified the royal character in the production.

gloves.definition: Garments covering the hands as part of a costume.
gloves.exampleUsage: The gloves covered the performer's hands.

stage-makeup.definition: Cosmetics applied to performers so facial features or character details are visible under stage lighting.
stage-makeup.exampleUsage: The stage makeup followed the character design.

face-paint.definition: Cosmetic paint designed for temporary decorative designs on the face.
face-paint.exampleUsage: The performer used face paint selected under the production's material requirements.

prop.definition: Any movable articles or objects used on the set of a play or movie.
prop.exampleUsage: The goblet was a prop used in the scene.

sword.definition: A cutting or thrusting weapon that has a long metal blade and a hilt with a hand guard.
sword.exampleUsage: The production uses an approved stage representation of a sword.

goblet.definition: A drinking glass with a base and stem.
goblet.exampleUsage: The performer placed the goblet on the table.

throne.definition: The chair of state for a monarch, bishop, etc.
throne.exampleUsage: The royal character sat on the stage throne.

table.definition: Furniture with a raised flat surface used on the stage.
table.exampleUsage: The table stood near the center of the set.

lantern.definition: A portable lamp used for light while camping.
lantern.exampleUsage: The lantern prop uses an approved simulated light effect.

banner.definition: A long piece of fabric or paper displaying words or images.
banner.exampleUsage: The banner formed part of the stage decoration.

treasure-chest.definition: A box designed to resemble a chest used for storing valuable objects, often used as a stage prop.
treasure-chest.exampleUsage: The painted treasure chest stood beside the set.

actor.definition: A performer portraying a character in a play; the term can apply to any gender.
actor.exampleUsage: The actor portrayed the main character.

actress.definition: A woman who performs a role in a film, play, or television show.
actress.exampleUsage: The actress performed the role during the evening show.

director.definition: The person guiding a theater production’s artistic interpretation and performance.
director.exampleUsage: The director discussed the scene's interpretation with the cast.

stage-manager.definition: The person coordinating rehearsal and performance operations.
stage-manager.exampleUsage: The stage manager coordinated the rehearsal schedule.

lighting-designer.definition: The theater professional who plans how stage lighting will look and change during a production.
lighting-designer.exampleUsage: The lighting designer planned the changes in illumination.

sound-technician.definition: A technician who sets up, monitors, and operates audio equipment for a performance or event.
sound-technician.exampleUsage: The sound technician monitored the microphones.

costume-designer.definition: The person who researches and creates the clothing concept for characters in a performance.
costume-designer.exampleUsage: The costume designer sketched clothing for the characters.

set-builder.definition: A worker who constructs scenery and physical stage-set elements from approved designs.
set-builder.exampleUsage: The set builder assembled scenery from the approved design.

prompter.definition: A person who assists a performer by providing the next words of a forgotten speech.
prompter.exampleUsage: The prompter supplied the next line when the performer needed assistance.

usher.definition: A person who helps audience members find their seats.
usher.exampleUsage: The usher helped the visitor find the booked seat.

rehearsal.definition: A practice session in preparation for a public performance (as of a play or speech or concert).
rehearsal.exampleUsage: The rehearsal prepared the cast for the performance.

opening-night.definition: It marks the first official public performance of a play, film, concert, or other production, after rehearsals or previews.
opening-night.exampleUsage: Opening night followed the rehearsal period.

monologue.definition: A (usually long) dramatic speech by a single actor.
monologue.exampleUsage: The character delivered a monologue without a spoken reply from another performer.

dialogue.definition: Spoken exchange between characters in a play.
dialogue.exampleUsage: The dialogue exchanged information between the characters.

scene.definition: A section of a play, often within an act.
scene.exampleUsage: The final scene resolves the play's central conflict.

act.definition: A major division of a play, often containing several scenes.
act.exampleUsage: The second act contains several scenes.

intermission.definition: The act of suspending activity temporarily.
intermission.exampleUsage: The intermission gave the audience a scheduled break.

standing-ovation.definition: A public display of strong approval occurs when an audience stands and applauds, usually to celebrate an outstanding performance, speech, or accomplishment.
standing-ovation.exampleUsage: Some audience members gave the cast a standing ovation.

encore.exampleUsage: The performers returned for an encore.

curtain-call.definition: A post-performance return to the stage allows actors or other performers to acknowledge the audience’s applause.
curtain-call.exampleUsage: The cast returned for the curtain call.

wing.definition: A stage area out of sight of the audience.
wing.exampleUsage: The stagehand waited in the wing beside the stage.

orchestra-pit.definition: A recessed musician area in front of a theater stage.
orchestra-pit.exampleUsage: The musicians played in the orchestra pit.

playwright.exampleUsage: The playwright wrote the dialogue and stage directions.

stagehand.definition: An employee of a theater who performs work involved in putting on a theatrical production.
stagehand.exampleUsage: The stagehand prepared the approved scenery for the next scene.

audience.definition: A gathering of spectators or listeners at a (usually public) performance.
audience.exampleUsage: The audience watched the performance from the auditorium.

understudy.definition: An actor able to replace a regular performer when required.
understudy.exampleUsage: The understudy prepared to replace the regular performer if required.

script.definition: The written dialogue and stage directions for a play.
script.exampleUsage: The script contains dialogue and stage directions.

makeup.definition: Cosmetics applied to the face to improve or change your appearance.
makeup.exampleUsage: The makeup altered the character's appearance.

ovation.definition: Enthusiastic recognition (especially one accompanied by loud applause).
ovation.exampleUsage: The audience gave the performers an enthusiastic ovation.

curtain.definition: A hanging fabric used to conceal or reveal the stage.
curtain.exampleUsage: The curtain concealed the stage before the opening scene.

apron.definition: The stage area extending in front of the proscenium opening.
apron.exampleUsage: The actor moved onto the apron in front of the proscenium.

robe.definition: A loose long garment used here as a costume.
robe.exampleUsage: The robe formed part of the character's costume.

chair.definition: A seat with a back, used here as stage furniture.
chair.exampleUsage: The chair stood beside the stage table.

candle.definition: An object producing light from a burning wick in wax; stage representations may use simulated effects.
candle.exampleUsage: The candle prop uses a simulated effect under venue arrangements.

mirror.definition: A surface that reflects an image.
mirror.exampleUsage: The performer checked the costume in the mirror.
